articles.excerpt: ACH Return Codes Explained: R01, R03, R10 and How to Handle Them When you're building a payout system, ACH returns are inevitable. A transaction you thought was settled comes back rejected, and you ne…
articles.body: ACH Return Codes Explained: R01, R03, R10 and How to Handle Them Understanding ACH Return Codes: A Developer's Guide When you're building a payout system, ACH returns are inevitable. A transaction you thought was settled comes back rejected, and you need to know why and what to do next . The National Automated Clearing House Association (Nacha) publishes a standardized set of return codes—R01 through R85—that tell you exactly what went wrong. This article breaks down the most common ones and how to handle them in code. The Big Three: R01, R03, and R10 R01: Insufficient Funds What it means: The recipient's account doesn't have enough money to cover the debit. This is the most common return code.

articles.title: Java4Shell: patching CVE-2026-114938 without breaking servers
articles.excerpt: The monitoring system just lit up with a CISA alert demanding an immediate fix for Java4Shell, a CVSS 9.2 vulnerability. Security engineers are telling everyone to roll out the -XX:UseAVX=2 flag acros…
articles.body: The monitoring system just lit up with a CISA alert demanding an immediate fix for Java4Shell, a CVSS 9.2 vulnerability. Security engineers are telling everyone to roll out the -XX:UseAVX=2 flag across all Java 17 and 21 microservices to prevent remote code execution. Blindly applying this parameter in a heterogeneous cluster will cause mass server crashes on ARM architecture. How 64 bytes break a 50-byte buffer Vulnerability CVE-2026-114938 lives inside the HotSpot JVM of OpenJDK. The Java virtual machine optimizes frequent operations. It swaps standard bytecode for platform-specific processor instructions. This mechanism is called intrinsics. When processing Base64, the virtual machine replaces the java.util.Base64 call with assembly code using AVX-512 VBMI vector instructions.
articles.author: Andrey Altrouter

articles.title: How to Set Up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for a New Domain (Step by Step)
articles.excerpt: You've bought a domain, set up hello@yourdomain.com, and sent your first email. Then it lands in spam. Or worse, it never arrives. Most of the time the fix is three DNS records: SPF, DKIM and DMARC. I…
articles.body: You've bought a domain, set up hello@yourdomain.com , and sent your first email. Then it lands in spam. Or worse, it never arrives. Most of the time the fix is three DNS records: SPF , DKIM and DMARC . I set these up for my own startup's domain recently, made a couple of mistakes along the way, and wrote down what actually worked. This guide walks through each record in the order you should add them. What these three records do (in one minute) Think of an email like a letter: SPF is a list of post offices allowed to send letters for your domain. DKIM is a wax seal on each letter that proves nobody changed it on the way. DMARC tells the receiving post office what to do if a letter fails those checks, and sends you reports about it.
articles.author: Prabhu Ganesan

Ak útočník dokáže do stránky vložiť cudzí skript (útok XSS), prehliadač ho vďaka CSP odmietne spustiť. Začnite prísne ( default-src 'self' ) a povoľujte len to, čo naozaj potrebujete. Vyhnite sa unsafe-inline pre skripty. Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) HSTS hovorí prehliadaču, aby sa na váš web pripájal vždy cez HTTPS, aj keď návštevník napíše http:// . articles.title: 66 Years Later, William Shatner's Forgotten 'Twilight Zone' Is Still a Haunting Masterpiece
articles.excerpt: The Twilight Zone episode “Nick of Time” is top-tier Shatner
articles.body: “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet” is one of the all-time great episodes of The Twilight Zone . Starring William Shatner, the story is about a man who is taking his first flight after having had a nervous breakdown. During the flight, he looks out the window and sees a creature, called a gremlin, on the wing that taunts him and tears apart pieces of the plane. No one can see the gremlin but him, and even his own wife attributes it to his fragile mental state. The story is a brilliant commentary on paranoia and Shatner was captivating in the role. It was so good that it sometimes overshadows Shatner’s other great episode of The Twilight Zone , which premiered 66 years ago today.

articles.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
articles.excerpt: Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.
articles.body: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers.

articles.excerpt: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the Un…
articles.body: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?

articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participant…
articles.body: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries.

articles.title: Space is filling up with junk. Could laser-reflecting mirrors help humanity clean things up?
articles.excerpt: The British company Foundational thinks its laser-reflecting tech can help humanity fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.
articles.body: A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem. Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit. Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years. Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors.
